name: Polyol pathway
summary: Glucose → sorbitol → fructose. Tissues with aldose reductase but little sorbitol dehydrogenase (lens, retina, Schwann cells, kidney) trap sorbitol in hyperglycemia → osmotic damage: cataracts, retinopathy, peripheral neuropathy. Liver, ovaries and seminal vesicles have both enzymes.

sorbitol.name: Sorbitol
sorbitol.notes: Osmotically active; can't cross membranes easily.

fructose.name: Fructose
fructose.notes: Seminal vesicles use this route to supply sperm with fructose.

ar.name: Aldose reductase
ar.notes: High in lens, retina, Schwann cells, kidney. Also reduces galactose to galactitol.

sdh.name: Sorbitol dehydrogenase
sdh.notes: Low or absent in lens, retina, Schwann cells and kidney — why sorbitol accumulates there.

tissue: lens, retina, Schwann cells, kidney (and liver, seminal vesicles)
